> 6 page(s) of developer.paypal.com documentation — Braintree — Docs — Guides under Google Pay. Part of the index one level up (../llms.txt).

## Google Pay

- [Overview](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/google-pay/overview): If you don't already accept Google Pay, you'll follow these steps to add a Google Pay button to your existing Braintree integration:
- [Configuration](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/google-pay/configuration/): Google Pay in the JavaScript SDK is available across multiple browsers.
- [Client-Side Implementation](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/google-pay/client-side/): Google Pay in the JavaScript SDK is available across multiple browsers. See for a full list.
- [Server-Side Implementation](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/google-pay/server-side/): Important Your integration may be impacted by upcoming certificate changes. Visit our
- [Testing and Go Live](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/google-pay/testing-go-live/): Google Pay in the JavaScript SDK is available across multiple browsers.
- [Client-Side Implementation](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/google-pay/client-side/android/v4): The SSL certificates for Braintree Mobile (iOS and Android) SDKs are set to expire on March 30, 2026.
